destination.name: Mount Gambier
destination.tagline: Crater lakes, sinkhole gardens and spring-fed ponds around a dormant volcano.
destination.description: Mount Gambier is the second most populated city in South Australia, built on the slopes of a dormant volcano about 450 km south-east of Adelaide and 17 km from the Victorian border. The Blue Lake and Valley Lake fill volcanic craters on its southern edge, while sinkholes open inside the city at the Cave Garden and Umpherston Sinkhole. Beyond town, Mount Schank's crater rim, the spring-fed ponds at Ewens and Piccaninnie, and the show cave at Tantanoola are day trips. Port MacDonnell, on the coast to the south, has the Cape Northumberland headland.
whyVisit: Peer into crater lakes and sinkholes

goodToKnow.title: Book Ewens snorkel permits
goodToKnow.detail: Every snorkel or dive at Ewens Ponds needs a permit booked before you arrive, and the ponds close to swimmers from 1 September to 30 November.

goodToKnow.title: Kilsby needs a booking
goodToKnow.detail: Kilsby Sinkhole is on a private working sheep farm, so you can enter only with a pre-booked tour, snorkel or dive.

goodToKnow.title: Tantanoola cave tickets
goodToKnow.detail: Park entry is free, but the cave tour is ticketed and can be booked online until midnight the day before. The cave is open daily 10 am to 3 pm.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} bring a deep turquoise Blue Lake and open snorkelling at Ewens Ponds.

Facts: second most populated city, 450 km from Adelaide, 17 km from Victoria (Wikipedia Mount Gambier); Blue Lake turquoise from November fading late Feb to March (Wikipedia Blue Lake / Warwar); Ewens closure 1 Sep to 30 Nov and permits (NPWS); Kilsby farm access (operator FAQ); Tantanoola hours and ticketing (NPWS).

Best months Dec-Mar picks the Blue Lake colour season and an open Ewens Ponds (closed Sep-Nov). Reasons: Piccaninnie water is closed until further notice so the snorkelling reason rests on Ewens and Kilsby.
